result.title: EgoLAM: Learning Latent Actions from Hand and Head Motion
result.summary: Latent action models let a robot policy learn from video by turning the change between two frames into a training target. In egocentric video, a cup can move across the image because a hand pushes it or because the wearer turns. Both changes help predict the next frame, but only the first describes manipulation. During training, EgoLAM supervises the action code with measured wrist motion and supplies camera motion separately to the forward model. Even when the wearer turns while pushing a cup, the training target still describes how the hand pushed it. The action encoder pools object slots around each hand, and wrist translation and rotation can be decoded from the code in a common reference frame. Extracting a code then requires only two RGB frames. Alongside LARYBench classification and regression, we measure how much wrist motion a frozen code retains and how strongly it responds to a synthetic view or lighting change. EgoLAM has the highest hand-motion decoding score among eight evaluated models. Across three LIBERO suites, policies pretrained on its codes and fine-tuned on expert demonstrations achieve 79.38% mean success, 28.73 points above expert behavior cloning and 9.76 points above the strongest other latent action model in each suite on average.

AI.brief_summary: EgoLAM 从第一视角视频的两帧图像中提取 latent action code，用实测手腕平移旋转作为监督信号，并把相机自身运动作为单独输入送入前向模型，从而把手部操作与视角变化解耦；在 LARYBench 与 LIBERO 上评估动作解码与策略预训练效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「任务相关动作信号 vs. 视角等无关变化」的显式分离，以及用冻结 code 探测手腕运动与合成视角、光照扰动的做法，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据筛选与 latent 内容保真度评价提供可供核查的线索；但属机器人动作表示，与 VLM 推理期状态生成距离较远。
